facts.text: Rozetka is one of the largest e-commerce companies in Ukraine, founded in 2005 in Kyiv by Vladyslav and Iryna Chechotkin.
Investment fund Horizon Capital became a co-owner of Rozetka in 2015, and the company has over 540 stores in more than 165 Ukrainian cities with over 5,000 employees.
Rozetka merged with marketplace operator EVO to expand its product range, IT infrastructure, and logistics capabilities.
Rozetka accelerated the restructuring of its business model to reduce self-managed retail sales and transition toward a decentralized network of smaller fulfillment hubs.
Commercial property owners in Ukraine have begun refusing to rent warehouse spaces to Rozetka due to risks of missile strikes.
Rozetka submitted proposals to Ukrainian authorities for post-strike tax deferrals and relief, which were rejected by the Ministry of Finance.
Rozetka's software platform is engineered around a microservices architecture supporting website features, automated warehouses, parcel lockers, and financial systems.
The core backend tech stack utilized by Rozetka includes PHP, Yii2, Redis, RabbitMQ, Docker, PostgreSQL, and Elasticsearch.
Rozetka advertises open technology roles, including backend engineering openings for PHP developers.
Vladyslav Chechotkin, Co-Founder and Chief Executive Officer
Rozetka lost its primary automated logistics and distribution center in Brovary to missile strikes, destroying facilities capable of processing over 100,000 orders daily.
The destruction created massive uninsured losses, delivery network disruptions, and reluctance among warehouse landlords to lease replacement facilities.
